assessment.nobel_worthiness: Empirical optimal taxation links the Mirrlees tradition of theory to measurable behavioural responses, namely the elasticity of taxable income and sufficient-statistics methods. It has shaped tax design and policy debate widely and has a clear, concrete policy payoff.
assessment.attribution: Slemrod is a foundational figure for taxable-income responses. Saez developed the bridge between optimal tax theory and elasticities. Chetty is central to the sufficient-statistics approach and quasi-experimental evidence. Stantcheva is influential but more recent, so I leave her out. Credit is shared with a large circle, and Chetty's work also appears in B021.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The core ideas date from the 1990s to 2010s and are widely replicated and applied by tax authorities and in policy design.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee prefers to honour the empirical-taxation core or a broader public-economics theme.
Overlap between Chetty's work here and in intergenerational mobility (B021).
Exact boundary of credit between Saez, Slemrod and Chetty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, with nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and interest-rate rules, underlies modern central-bank practice and policy modelling. It is among the most influential macroeconomic frameworks in use.
assessment.attribution: The credit is spread across many people. Calvo supplied time-dependent pricing, Taylor the staggered contracts and policy rule, and Woodford the systematic, welfare-based synthesis. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets made important contributions that a three-person limit cannot capture. This is the hardest candidate on which to draw a defensible line.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of use in policy and a robust empirical and theoretical literature.
uncertainties: Attribution is contested among eight listed names, and the choice of three is sensitive.
Possible reluctance to honour macro-policy frameworks after recent macroeconomic prizes.
Debate over the empirical adequacy of the baseline model after the post-2020 inflation episode.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-firm trade models changed how the field thinks about selection, reallocation and the gains from trade. They moved the field from the representative-firm world to one grounded in firm-level microdata. Their influence on theory, empirics and policy analysis is large.
assessment.attribution: Melitz's 2003 model is the core contribution, and Helpman's wider theory of trade with firm heterogeneity builds on and extends it. Redding is important for quantitative extensions but is the least necessary name for a core prize. A two-person award is cleaner. Krugman's 2008 prize partly covered adjacent ground.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with over two decades of confirmation and extension, including empirical work on firm-level data.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier Krugman prize and with Helpman's role in B041.
Whether the Committee views this as incremental to new trade theory.
Whether Redding should be included.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Present bias, quasi-hyperbolic discounting and reference dependence are central to behavioural models of saving, consumption and self-control. They feed into policy design such as defaults and commitment devices. The work is strongly theoretical and has been tested empirically.
assessment.attribution: Laibson is closely tied to quasi-hyperbolic discounting and its macro and finance applications, and Rabin to the formalisation of behavioural preferences, including present bias with O'Donoghue and reference dependence with Koszegi. Loewenstein, Koszegi and O'Donoghue are also notable, so the cut is somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with strong field-level uptake, though behavioural economics has already been recognised through Kahneman and Thaler.
uncertainties: Possible view that behavioural economics has been adequately recognised.
The credit boundary among five names.
Mixed replication of some reference-dependence predictions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the analysis of import-competition shocks reshaped understanding of wage inequality and the local labour-market effects of trade and automation. The work is highly policy-relevant and widely cited.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the common thread across the task-based and trade-shock work. Hanson is central to the China-shock empirical agenda with Autor and Dorn. Katz's wider contributions are partly captured elsewhere. The task framework also draws on Acemoglu and others, who are outside this ballot.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. The China-shock findings are recent enough that long-run interpretation continues to evolve, though the influence is clear.
uncertainties: Debates over the magnitude and persistence of the trade-shock effects.
Overlap with the 2024 recognition of Acemoglu's technology work.
Whether two or three names best reflect the contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative Ricardian and gravity-based models gave a tractable, empirically disciplined method of computing gains from trade and the effects of trade policy. The approach is widely used in applied trade policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Kortum is credited through the Eaton–Kortum framework, though Eaton is not on this ballot, which weakens any prize on the underlying model. Costinot and Rodriguez-Clare are key for the quantitative implementations and the sufficient-statistics gains-from-trade formulas.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. The framework has been established for over two decades, but part of the credit lies outside the listed names.
uncertainties: The Eaton–Kortum framework requires Jonathan Eaton, who is not listed.
Competition from the heterogeneous-firm tradition in B010.
Dependence on structural modelling assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model gave a strategic foundation for bargaining and underpins work in game theory, labour, search and market models. It is a major contribution to microeconomic theory with a decisive influence on later work.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein's 1982 model is the clear core. Wolinsky is important for market bargaining with decentralised trade, and Binmore for the broader programme and implementation. A sole laureate gives the cleanest attribution.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with more than four decades of confirmation and an enduring role in the theory.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee considers the game-theory area sufficiently honoured by past prizes.
Whether Wolinsky or Binmore should share the credit.
Rubinstein's later work moved toward methodology and bounded rationality, which may change perceptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design opened a research programme on how an informed sender can optimally shape beliefs. It connects to mechanism and market design, disclosure, regulation and platform design.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow originated the Bayesian persuasion model. Morris, with Bergemann, is central to information design and robust mechanism design. Bergemann is a plausible alternative or additional name.
assessment.maturity: Relatively young. The formal framework dates from 2011, and long-run empirical or practical validation is still limited.
uncertainties: Whether applications are yet sufficiently demonstrated.
Credit split between persuasion and information design.
Timing may be early compared with other candidates.
